indexes._comment: Index 1 — Direct children query (parentId + isArchived + order)
Index 2 — Subtree query via ancestorIds array-contains
Index 3 — Assignee node lookup with status + dueDate sort
Index 5 — Tasks subcollection: assignee collectionGroup query (Phase 16)
Index 6 — History subcollection: recent activity collectionGroup (Phase 16+17)
Index 7 — Tasks subcollection: nodeId + dueDate for calendar dedup (Phase 15)

_fieldOverrides_comment: DANGER: `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` treats this array as the COMPLETE set of single-field overrides. Any override that exists in the project but is missing here is DELETED. Adding one field here therefore silently drops every other field's exemption — which is exactly how the tasks.assignedTo entry below got removed once, breaking the employee dashboard in production. Never add an entry without checking what is already live: npx firebase-tools firestore:indexes

fieldOverrides._comment: TaskContext.jsx runs collectionGroup('tasks').where('assignedTo','array-contains',uid) with no other filter. A single-field array-contains query is NOT served by composite index 5 (assignedTo + status) — it needs its own CONTAINS index, and the automatic ones are COLLECTION-scoped only, so the COLLECTION_GROUP entry is required. The first three restate the automatic defaults, which declaring an override replaces.

roadmapDeadlineCheck's 'due tomorrow' scan is a dueDate range over collectionGroup('tasks'). Collection-group queries are not served by the automatic single-field indexes, which are COLLECTION-scoped only, so dueDate needs an explicit COLLECTION_GROUP entry. The two COLLECTION entries below are the defaults, restated because declaring an override replaces them.
